actions.reason: The K3_C0002-K3_C0003 boundary is weakly and inconsistently represented: all four native geometries show small positive mean silhouettes (CT 0.060, WXS 0.044, WSI 0.043, RNA 0.041) with substantial negative fractions (WSI 0.568, WXS 0.419, RNA 0.338, CT 0.257) and a negative WSI median, and K3_C0003 is the nearest competing set for K3_C0002 in all four views. Structurally, the union eigengap is single-cluster-dominated (candidate_k=1, leading gap 0.488 vs k=2 gap 0.329), the two-way spectral partition agrees only moderately with current labels (ARI 0.698), and the normalized-cut cost is relatively high (0.592), indicating substantial cross-boundary connectivity. Together these constitute a coherent merge-compatible pattern for re-review of the union K3_C0002∪K3_C0003.

actions.reason: K3_C0001 has a substantively interpretable biological identity: RNA shows a coherent, strongly enriched immune/inflammatory plus proliferation program (multiple pathways at fdr_q=0.001, large |NES|), and WXS shows a directionally consistent BAP1-enriched ccRCC-associated mutation phenotype (OR 7.88, q_driver 0.018). Membership representation is weak-to-modest but positive in CT, RNA, and WXS (mean silhouettes 0.023, 0.137, 0.057), with WSI showing no separation; the pair boundary against K3_C0002_M_K3_C0003 is weakly but consistently represented in CT, RNA, and WSI (silhouettes 0.087, 0.079, 0.130) with WXS showing none. The pair structural screen is merge-compatible (union eigengap dominated at k=1, ARI 0.004, normalized-cut 0.713), but merge is not an available structural action in this round, and the internal-subdivision screen does not support a feasible split (leading eigengap at k=1; k=2/k=3 children imbalanced with weak or near-zero native-view separation). Candidate-specific technical associations (tissue source site, CT scanner model, CT z-spacing, CT slice thickness) remain plausible alternative explanations, but no available evidence request could test whether these factors are reflected in the relevant patient geometry, so this cannot be resolved further this round. Given the strong, coherent biological identity and the absence of a supported split or an available merge, K3_C0001 remains a defensible independent discovery-stage unit.

K3_C0002_M_K3_C0003 has a substantively interpretable biological identity: RNA shows a coherent transcriptomic phenotype reciprocal to K3_C0001 (down-regulated immune/inflammatory and proliferation programs, up-regulated metabolism/androgen programs, multiple pathways at fdr_q=0.001 with large |NES|), and WXS shows a directionally consistent BAP1-depleted mutation phenotype (OR 0.127, q_driver 0.018). Membership representation is weak-to-modest but positive in CT, RNA, and WSI (mean silhouettes 0.112, 0.056, 0.190), with WXS showing no separation; the pair boundary against K3_C0001 is weakly but consistently represented in CT, RNA, and WSI (silhouettes 0.087, 0.079, 0.130) with WXS showing none. The pair structural screen is merge-compatible (union eigengap dominated at k=1, ARI 0.004, normalized-cut 0.713), but merge is not an available structural action in this round, and the internal-subdivision screen does not support a feasible split (leading eigengap at k=1; the balanced k=2 split shows only modest consensus separation with weak native-view separation, and k=3/k=4 are near-zero or negative in CT, RNA, and WSI). Candidate-specific technical associations (tissue source site, CT scanner model, CT z-spacing, CT slice thickness) remain plausible alternative explanations, but no available evidence request could test whether these factors are reflected in the relevant patient geometry, so this cannot be resolved further this round. Given the strong, coherent biological identity and the absence of a supported split or an available merge, this set remains a defensible independent discovery-stage unit.
